Purpose and scope

and securely. It applies to every device, account and system Alderbridge provides or permits access
through, and to every employee, agency worker, contractor and volunteer with any level of access.

Policy statement

IT systems at Alderbridge exist to support safe, high-quality care, not as a general convenience to be used
however an individual sees fit; this policy balances that operational purpose with a reasonable, trusted
allowance for ordinary personal use, and is enforced consistently rather than selectively.

Definitions

otherwise provides for work use. **Acceptable use** use that is lawful, does not breach any other

limited, reasonable use of a work system for non-work purposes, permitted subject to the conditions in this
policy. **Privileged access** any account with elevated permissions beyond an ordinary user account,
such as an IT administrator account.

security concern to the IT service desk immediately. **IT** maintains technical controls (password policy,
antivirus, monitoring) and investigates any reported or detected concern. **Line managers** address a
minor misuse concern informally in the first instance, escalating a serious concern to HR under the
Disciplinary Procedure.

Phishing Awareness: Spotting a Suspicious Email

Purpose and scope

These guidance notes help staff recognise and respond to phishing attempts. They apply to every employee using an Alderbridge email account or system.

Policy statement

Phishing is one of the most common ways an organisation's systems are compromised, and Alderbridge treats every member of staff as a genuine, valued part of its defence against it, not merely a risk to be trained around.

Definitions

**Phishing** a fraudulent attempt, usually by email, to obtain sensitive information or trick someone into an unsafe action by impersonating a trusted sender. **Spear phishing** a phishing attempt specifically targeted at a named individual or organisation using researched, personalised detail. **Business email compromise** a phishing variant impersonating a colleague or supplier, often requesting an urgent payment or data transfer.

Roles and responsibilities

**Every member of staff** reports a suspected phishing email using the 'Report Phishing' function, or by forwarding it to the IT service desk, and never clicks a suspicious link or attachment. **IT** investigates every report, blocks the sender where appropriate, and alerts other staff if a campaign is targeting Alderbridge specifically.

Check the sender's actual email address, not just the display name, since a display name can be easily forged.

Be suspicious of urgent or threatening language demanding immediate action, a hallmark of many phishing attempts.

Never click a link or open an attachment from an unexpected or suspicious email; hover over a link to see its real destination before clicking, if genuinely uncertain.

Never provide a password, bank detail, or make a payment based solely on an email request, however senior the apparent sender.

Phishing is not limited to email; a fraudulent QR code (sometimes called 'quishing') or a suspicious text message asking you to click a link or call a number follows the same underlying pattern and the same response — do not scan, click or call, and report it to IT the same way as a suspicious email, since the delivery method changes but the underlying red flags (urgency, an unexpected request, a mismatched sender) remain the same across every channel.

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Purpose and scope

This guidance sets out the password and account access standard for every Alderbridge system. It applies to every member of staff with a login to any Alderbridge system.

Policy statement

A strong, personal password kept confidential is one of the simplest and most effective protections for resident data and Alderbridge systems generally.

Definitions

Personal Data Breach Procedure

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds to a suspected or confirmed personal data
breach, under the UK GDPR's own breach-notification requirements. It applies to any incident involving
personal data — a lost device, a misdirected email, unauthorised access, or a genuine cyber incident —
regardless of how minor it initially appears.

Policy statement

Alderbridge treats a fast, honest internal report of a suspected breach as far more valuable than a delayed,
polished one, and this procedure is deliberately built around a very short internal reporting window, since
the regulatory 72-hour clock for a notifiable breach starts running from when Alderbridge becomes aware
of it, not from when the investigation concludes.

Definitions

**Personal data breach** a breach of security leading to the accidental or unlawful destruction, loss,
alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data. **Notifiable breach** a breach likely to
result in a risk to individuals' rights and freedoms, requiring notification to the Information Commissioner's
Office within 72 hours of Alderbridge becoming aware of it. **High-risk breach** a breach likely to result in
a high risk to individuals, additionally requiring the affected individuals themselves to be notified without
undue delay. **Containment** the immediate action taken to stop a breach continuing or worsening (for
example, recalling a misdirected email, or disabling a compromised account).

Confidentiality and data protection

Frequently asked questions

**Can I look up a friend's relative's records if they ask me to check on their care?** No — this is exactly the
curiosity-access scenario this policy prohibits; direct them to the person's own registered manager instead.
**Is it a breach if a resident's name is visible on a whiteboard in the staff area?** It depends on who can
see the whiteboard; a staff-only area used for handover is generally acceptable, but a whiteboard visible to
visitors or other residents is not, and site managers are expected to check this specifically as part of their

Report it the same way as any other suspected breach, however small it feels — the Data Protection Lead,

Video calls and screen sharing while working remotely

During a video call or screen share involving sensitive information, staff confirm no unauthorised person can view or overhear the call, close any unrelated sensitive document before sharing a screen, and use only Alderbridge-approved conferencing tools rather than a personal account on an unapproved platform, applying the same care to a video meeting as to an in-person conversation about the same information.

Wi-Fi security at an approved home location

Ending a remote working arrangement

Where a remote working arrangement ends, whether by the employee's own request or a genuine business need, IT confirms the issued device and any remote access credential are returned or revoked promptly, following the same access-removal discipline the IT Acceptable Use Policy sets out for a leaver, since a remote arrangement ending is functionally similar to a change of access requirement even where employment itself continues.

Backing up work created while working remotely

Work saved locally on a remote device, rather than directly to an Alderbridge system, is backed up regularly using the approved method IT provides, since a device fault or loss while working remotely should never result in genuinely lost work, and staff are shown how to confirm their own backup is actually running correctly as part of their remote working setup.

Family members and household members during remote work

A family or household member should never have access to an Alderbridge device or account, even briefly and even for an unrelated purpose such as checking their own personal email, since this creates an unnecessary and entirely avoidable risk to data the household member has no reason to see.

IT and Communications Acceptable Use Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how staff use Alderbridge Care Group's IT and communications systems responsibly
and securely. It applies to every device, account and system Alderbridge provides or permits access
through, and to every employee, agency worker, contractor and volunteer with any level of access.

Policy statement

IT systems at Alderbridge exist to support safe, high-quality care, not as a general convenience to be used
however an individual sees fit; this policy balances that operational purpose with a reasonable, trusted
allowance for ordinary personal use, and is enforced consistently rather than selectively.

Definitions

**Alderbridge system** any device, account, application or network Alderbridge owns, licenses or
otherwise provides for work use. **Acceptable use** use that is lawful, does not breach any other
Alderbridge policy, and does not create an unreasonable security or reputational risk. **Personal use**
limited, reasonable use of a work system for non-work purposes, permitted subject to the conditions in this
policy. **Privileged access** any account with elevated permissions beyond an ordinary user account,
such as an IT administrator account.

**Every member of staff** uses Alderbridge systems in line with this policy and reports any suspected
security concern to the IT service desk immediately. **IT** maintains technical controls (password policy,
antivirus, monitoring) and investigates any reported or detected concern. **Line managers** address a
minor misuse concern informally in the first instance, escalating a serious concern to HR under the
Disciplinary Procedure.
